NFR1 is canonically Performance and governs latency budgets and bounded work over a store of 10,000 analyses; this unit reads no store, has no route, and its operations are linear in their own input. An earlier draft keyed the security requirements here — that was a numbering shift, corrected to NFR2 below.

security-requirements.md NFR2.1–NFR2.6 — the offline guarantee, the credential exclusion, the fan-out-0 isolation, the no-I/O purity, the untrusted-input treatment and the in-repo stopword set. Two of those six name work that does NOT yet exist: no ast import-closure check and no credential scanner are in the repository. The DoS discussion records an open gap — nothing bounds the size of a stored text column, upstream or here.

not applicable to a library. The parent governs /v1 behaviour freeze and the SentimentClient interface; this unit is new code with no versioned surface. It touches no existing behaviour except through BR5.1's parity obligation, which is an NFR6 concern.

rules.md BR4.5 and BR6.1 — module-level typed constants in SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE, a docstring, full annotations, __future__ import, underscore-private helpers and no utils/helpers file. The conventions apply to every new module, and this one is the smaller of the two.

tests/test_terms.py — ten tests that reach the real module and never mock it: tokenisation by hand-read cases, the absence of a length or stopword filter in tokenize, order and repeat preservation, the all-stopword empty case, the sentiment-word exclusion in the stopword set, the single-tokeniser guarantee, engine scoring parity, the exhaustive pattern-parity check, and the engine's tokenize-only consumption. An earlier draft marked this N/A because the parent is stated in terms of SQLite and markup; that is the feature-level framing, not the parent's subject, and the review caught the over-broad read.
